problem: Dropping the closed-lower-bound-first tie-breaker lets an open-start interval be merged first, so merge() (line 73) refuses a join with a left neighbour that only touches at a closed start, and normalize/union return split, input-order-dependent output such as normalize([(-1,0,T,F),(0,1,F,F),(0,0,T,T)]) -> [(-1,0,T,F),(0,1,T,F)] instead of [(-1,1,T,F)].
The branch changes the canonical sort order without any test covering same-start intervals with mixed closedness in both input orders, so nothing catches the F1 regression.

Pre-existing: is_number accepts NaN and is_empty treats NaN intervals as non-empty, so NaN bounds reach the sort and merge and silently corrupt results (e.g. normalize([(nan,1),(0,2)]) -> [(nan,2,T,T)]).

Pre-existing: validate_bounds rejects a closed end only when the bound is None, so an explicit closed -inf/+inf is accepted and exported as a closed None end, breaking the rule that unbounded ends are open.
